newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian economy up modestly, says central bank.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian economy up modestly, says central bank.

text.p: Nigeria's central bank said the nation's economy showed some improvement in the first half of 1996 but was cautious on the outlook for the rest of the year.
"The performance of the real sector improved modestly," the central bank said in its mid-year review, referring to agricultural and industrial production.
"By June, 1996 there were strong indications that agricultural production had improved further and would be sustained for the rest of the year," it added.
Industrial activity also picked up moderately and there was a rise in crude oil output, Nigeria's economic lifeblood, while inflation was down.
Economists broadly agreed with the report but said the modest improvement was yet to show in the lives of ordinary people.

"There is stability of macro-economic sectors. What remains to be seen is when people will begin to feel it in terms of jobs and affordability of essential commodities," said Bisi Ogunde of Lagos state university.

Military-ruled Nigeria, which slumped into crisis in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential election, has put in place liberal economic policies that have seen the exchange rate stabilise and inflation head downwards.
But so far this has failed to attract foreign investment and the government has begun to campaign aggressively for investors.

The central bank report said the country recorded a budget deficit of 6.577 billion naira ($82.2 million) in the first half of 1996 which contrasts with an eight billion naira surplus declared for the same period last month by Finance Minister Anthony Ani.
The difference between the two stemmed from conflicting figures for debt servicing.
The central bank warned against increased money supply, saying this could affect the country's economic performance.

"The resurgence of excess liquidity in banks could constrain the sustainability of the observed favourable developments," it said, adding that "Consequently, the outlook for the rest of the year, should be viewed with cautious optimism."
It said Nigeria's foreign debt declined marginally to $31.996 billion at the end of June 1996 from 32.581 billion at the end of 1995.

"Total actual external debt service payments during the first half of 1996 amounted to $1.215 billion which represented only 23 percent of the projected annual debt service payment due," the bank said.
External assets, however, shot to $5.174 billion at the end of June 1996 from $3.137 billion at the end of June 1995.
Bankers said the accumulation was a direct result of high prices for crude oil, which accounts for 90 percent of the country's foreign income.
